title: TG#1 = composite + full frame (2 photos, real MIME)
author: the operator
trigger: operator directive 2026-09-09 ~12:32: 'Well, I don't see a pairwise differential composite at all, and the crops don't look like they're being done well. Period. We have a perfectly working example in the refactor version 1 of how they're supposed to be.' Follow-up directive 2026-09-09 ~12:45: 'This is when Telegram alert 1 should go out with one of the full images, and the pairwise differential image, along with the positions in the four images'. The motivation: today's TG#1 attaches 5 photos (best_frame + diff_image + 4 frame paths) which (a) overwhelms the operator's chat, (b) repeats what's already on camera 4 times, (c) has a known MIME bug where dispatcher forces 'image/png' on JPEG bytes. The refactor version 1's TG#1 sends ONE composite (median + red motion + green bbox) at native resolution as a single PNG via sendPhoto. v2 needs the same.
background: telegram_formatter/alert.py:65-70 currently builds photos = [best_frame] + [diff_image] + frame_paths -- a 5-element list of paths. Of those 5: (1) is best_frame (frame_paths[3]), (2) is the gate's diff_image (which doesn't exist on disk for the current pipeline because GATE_KEEP_DISK_ARTIFACTS=false), (3-6) are the 4 raw frames. telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py:88 forces `mime='image/png'` + filename=`photo_i.png` on every attachment regardless of file content -- this is the source of the Telegram MIME bug. PRD-V2-027 has three jobs: (1) alert.py emits a 2-photo list `[composite_path, full_frame_path]` from artifacts (PRD-V2-024 produces these), (2) dispatcher.py sniffs file bytes to determine the real MIME type, (3) caption text on TG#1 lists the 4-frame positions (operator's directive 'along with the positions in the four images').
shipping_definition: All US-027 stories marked done; pytest 150/150 (or higher) green; tree clean; alert.py build_alert_message returns photos = [composite_path, full_frame_path]; dispatcher.py MIME type is sniffed from file bytes (`image/png` for PNGs, `image/jpeg` for JPEGs, fallback `application/octet-stream` only for genuinely unknown types with a logged warning); caption text on TG#1 mentions the 4 frame positions; manual smoke test against the real Telegram group -5264050975 produces a 2-photo TG#1 with the composite and the full frame visible side-by-side in the chat; no MIME error in Telegram's response.
scope_exclusions: Editing telegram_formatter/detail.py is NOT this PRD -- TG#2 already sends the right two crops. Verified by reading detail.py:71-74 already returns [crop_a_path, crop_b_path] which is correct per the operator.
Editing telegram_formatter/match_alert.py is NOT this PRD -- TG#3 is text-only and that is correct.
Renaming or refactoring the Telegram bot API wrapper is NOT this PRD -- only the photo-list-construction in alert.py and the MIME-sniffing in dispatcher.py.
Switching from sendMediaGroup to sendPhoto (or vice versa) is NOT this PRD -- whatever the dispatcher does today, it continues to do. The list size is what changes.
Adding a fallback MIME 'always use image/png no matter what' is FORBIDDEN by design_principles. If sniffing fails, log + use 'application/octet-stream'.
Compressing the composite before sending is NOT this PRD -- the composite is sent at native camera resolution as a single PNG. (Refactor proves this works within Telegram's size limit.)
design_principles: TG#1 sends exactly 2 photos: the composite (composite.png) and the full frame (frame_paths[3]). No 4-frame flood, no diff_image fallback.

The dispatcher MIME type matches the file's actual bytes. Sniffing is cheap (read first 16 bytes), and the resulting MIME is what the bot sends. PNG's magic is `89 50 4E 47`; JPEG's is `FF D8 FF`; an unknown first-bytes-pattern logs a warning and uses 'application/octet-stream' (no fallback to image/png -- that was the bug).
Telegram's sendMediaGroup (or sendPhoto) accepts native-resolution images; the operator wants full fidelity. No thumbnail generation, no width clamp -- the bot library decides.

The caption text lists frame positions: 'frames: t-3, t-2, t-1, t0 (positions: x,y,w,h for each)'. The positions are the subject bboxes from the gate (gate_verdict.crop_bbox_a, gate_verdict.crop_bbox_b). If bboxes are None, the caption says 'no subject bbox detected'.

TG#1 message structure: 2 photos in a single sendMediaGroup call, with caption text on the first photo. The caption is concise: <subject_classification> at <relative_time_now>, with summary of what was visible. The operator refines this language in a follow-up story.

The dispatcher test uses a few synthetic files: PNG with PNG magic bytes asserts mime=image/png; JPEG with JFIF bytes asserts mime=image/jpeg; a file with garbage bytes logs warning + mime=application/octet-stream.
No fallback when build_alert_message raises. The error propagates; the pipeline's stage 11 catches it and decides whether to call record_hit (per PRD-V2-026c, TG#1 failure -> NO record_hit).

stories.title: alert.py: 2 photos from artifacts (composite + full frame)
acceptance: telegram_formatter/alert.py:build_alert_message consumes alert['artifacts'] (from PRD-V2-024).
It returns photos = [alert['artifacts'].composite_path, alert['artifacts'].frame_paths[3]] IF alert['artifacts'].composite_path is not None.
If composite_path is None (gate returned no bbox), return photos = [alert['artifacts'].frame_paths[3]] only -- single photo, NOT 1-photo-then-3-fallback.
The 4 raw-frame paths are NO LONGER attached to TG#1. They are deleted from alert.py's photo-list construction.
The diff_image path (the gate's pairwise_diff.jpg) is NO LONGER referenced by alert.py. The variable `diff_image` is removed.
The best_frame alias to frame_paths[3] is explicit (frame_paths[3] reads cleanly enough; best_frame alias may stay if it improves readability, but not strictly required).
tests/test_alert_message.py exists with at least 3 cases: (a) full artifacts -> photos=[composite, full], (b) composite=None -> photos=[full], (c) frame_paths missing -> raises (no silent fill-in).
Existing test_pipeline.py mocks of build_alert_message still pass with the new signature.
Single commit: 'alert.py: TG#1 photos=[composite, full] from artifacts (US-027a)'.
pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_home_env.py still 150/150 (or higher) green.

stories.title: dispatcher.py: sniff file bytes for real MIME
acceptance: telegram_formatter/dispatcher.py:88 currently forces mime='image/png' regardless of file content. Replace with a _sniff_mime(path) helper that reads the first 16 bytes.
_sniff_mime returns 'image/png' for PNG magic, 'image/jpeg' for JPEG magic, 'application/octet-stream' for unknown (with a logger.warning), 'image/jpeg' (mime-correct) for JPEGs.
Filename suffix matches the actual MIME: `.png` for PNG, `.jpg` for JPEG. NOT `.png` for everything.

Test test_sniff_mime.py exists with at least 4 cases: (a) /tmp/foo.png with PNG bytes -> image/png, (b) /tmp/foo.jpg with JPEG bytes -> image/jpeg, (c) /tmp/foo.txt with ASCII bytes -> application/octet-stream + logger.warning, (d) empty file -> application/octet-stream + logger.warning.
The original 'image/png' hardcode is REMOVED (no fallback). The new code path raises logger.warning on unknown and uses octet-stream -- exactly once per file per webhook.
Existing tests that asserted the old hardcoded 'image/png' behavior fail to compile if they exist -- they get updated to assert the new correct behavior.
Single commit: 'dispatcher.py: sniff file bytes for real MIME (US-027b)'.
pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/test_home_env.py still 150/150 (or higher) green.

stories.title: caption text lists 4-frame positions on TG#1
acceptance: telegram_formatter/alert.py:build_alert_message composes a caption string.

Caption includes: classification (from gate_verdict.classification), top_class + top_confidence, camera_id, alert_id, timestamp, and the 4-frame positions formatted as 'frames[t-3]: (x,y,w,h), frames[t-2]: (x,y,w,h), frames[t-1]: (x,y,w=h), frames[t0]: (x,y,w,h)'.
If the gate did not produce bboxes (gate_verdict.crop_bbox_a is None), the position line says 'no subject bbox detected'.
Caption length does not exceed Telegram's 1024-character caption limit. (Cap if needed; refactor's caption was ~600 chars.)

Tests test_alert_message_caption.py exist with at least 3 cases: (a) full bbox -> caption includes 4 positions, (b) no bbox -> caption says 'no subject bbox detected', (c) long top_class string -> caption is truncated to <=1024 chars (with ellipsis on the truncated portion).
Single commit: 'alert.py caption lists 4-frame positions (US-027c)'.
pytest still green.

stories.title: live smoke to -5264050975 group verifies 2-photo TG#1
acceptance: Operator confirms via ask: 'set up a synthetic webhook and tell me when TG#1 lands'.

Assistant: (1) reader frame is touched to bypass mtime cutoff, (2) synthetic Reolink-shaped webhook is sent to localhost:8090 with the camera_id matching a real channel that YOLO can see, (3) the daemon returns alert_id, (4) the pipeline runs to completion, (5) the TG#1 message lands in chat -5264050975 with 2 visible photos.
Manual or screenshot verification: TG#1 message has composite.png + frame_004.jpg visible at native resolution, caption present, no 'image/png' error from Telegram's API.
If TG#1 fails to send, the failure is logged but does NOT block this PRD -- that's a debugging session, not a PRD gate.
Single commit OR no commit (this is verification, code may not change) -- captured in logs/daemon.log.
Output to operator: 'TG#1 confirmed in -5264050975 with 2 photos and correct MIME.'
